headline: Day four of the squeeze broadened to everything except the things that matter: SOXX +7.5% with NVDA -4.3%, Brent down to 90.12, ETH -3.5%, and VIX back up to 20.28.
summary: Geography kept carrying the bounce — KOSPI +4.4%, Nikkei +2.9% to 60,460, TAIEX +2.5%, DAX +1.2% at the 100th percentile of its year, CAC +1.2%, Euro Stoxx +1.1% — and FX paid in the right places again (USD/KRW -1.6%, EUR +0.3% to 1.1186, AUD +0.6%, CEW turning up) with DXY barely changed at 101.8. But the risk regime slipped back to -11 from -10, and the leadership inside the squeeze changed in a way that matters. SOXX +7.5% and SMH +5.1% were powered by AMD +13.3%, AVGO +8.8%, MU +6.3%, ASML +6.2% — while NVDA fell 4.3%, is -22.1% on the month, sits in the 19th percentile of its 52-week range and 12.6% below its 200-day with relative strength -19.4%. A semi rally the generals don't join is short covering, not a cycle turn.

The invoice keeps getting bigger and nobody is paying it. Investment-grade OAS 0.93 at z=1.59 with acceleration +0.93, BBB 1.16 at z=1.68 with acceleration +0.86 — 95th-96th percentile of the year and still widening through a +2.3% S&P session. HY 3.42 (+33bp on the month, 93rd percentile), CCC 13.17 (+88bp on the month, +432bp YTD). HYG is +0.4% over the month and has marked none of it; HYG/IEF z=-1.66. Against that, VIX rose 1.8% to 20.28 (z=1.41, turning up) and the term structure at 0.9554 is out of inversion with SKEW at 150 — protection is cheap at exactly the moment high-grade credit is deteriorating fastest. The credit & vol composite is -48, by far the ugliest reading on the board.

The cycle itself keeps voting against the tape. Brent -2.6% to 90.12 (-13.0% on the week, -13.9% on the month), WTI 84.93, RBOB -21.0% on the month at z=-1.94, copper -0.8% and -5.5% on the month, gold/silver +12.3% on the month at z=1.82, DBC -6.0%. Energy equities still refuse to mark crude: XLE is only -4.8% on the month, +41.3% YTD, 5.6% above its 200-day; XOP -9.1% against Brent's -13.9%. Cheap crude is showing up in breakevens (5y 2.25, 16th percentile; 10y 2.22, 12th) but not in funding: the 2-year backed up 5bp to 4.51, 10y 4.86, 10y real 2.63 in the 74th percentile, mortgage 7.18%, 2s10s 32bp at the 22nd percentile and 3m10y -35bp on the month. Housing starts -5.2%, UMich 48.1. Plumbing stays thin — RRP is effectively zero at $0.25bn, reserves -2.1% over three months, net liquidity rolling over.

Both non-confirmations flagged yesterday got worse, not better. Crypto put in a second straight down day and accelerated: ETH -3.5% to 2,058 (-18.8% on the month), SOL -3.4% (-24.8%), BTC -1.9% to 73,798, ETH/BTC at the 20th percentile, COIN at the 0.7th percentile of its year, MSTR -18.6% on the month. Brazil deteriorated on a flat-dollar day: USD/BRL +1.1% to 5.5653, z=3.14 with acceleration +2.38, EWZ -25.1% on the month, Bovespa acceleration -3.84 — against India compounding (INDA +11.7%, acceleration +2.76, USD/INR -3.0% at z=-2.91) and Mexico's IPC at the 100th percentile. Under the hood the regime is unmoved: RSP/SPY z=3.59 with acceleration 3.28, growth/value at the 7th percentile, MTUM z=-3.01, high-beta/low-vol z=-2.91. HD +21.6%, MCD +19.6%, LLY +19.7%, UPS +17.3% on the month versus GOOGL -18.1%, CAT -25.0%, ORCL -15.3%. Rent the squeeze, own the rotation — and today the hedge is cheaper than the chase.

good.text: Breadth is the real bull market: equal-weight/cap-weight at z=3.59 with acceleration 3.28, SPW +3.7% on the month against the S&P's -3.3%, IWM +3.2% on the day and turning up, midcaps +1.3%.
The squeeze went global and the FX side confirmed it: KOSPI +4.4%, Nikkei +2.9%, TAIEX +2.5%, DAX +1.2% at the 100th percentile, with USD/KRW -1.6% and the EM currency basket turning up.
The long end has given back real money over the month — 10y -42bp, 30y -41bp, TLT +5.1% — and MOVE fell 7.3% to 85.98, so bond vol is not the source of the stress.

Labour and activity data are still clean: initial claims 189k at the 0th percentile of the year, unemployment 4.1% (-10bp), JOLTS openings +4.6%, industrial production and capacity utilisation at 52-week highs.
Disinflation is being priced where it counts: 5y breakevens 2.25 (16th percentile), 10y 2.22 (12th), gasoline -21.0% on the month at z=-1.94.
Defensive and domestic leadership keeps compounding: XLV +10.3% on the month (rel +14.1%), medical devices z=2.50, financials rel +9.6%, retail rel +14.1%, homebuilders/S&P z=2.87.

bad.text: High-grade credit widened through a +2.3% S&P day and is accelerating: IG OAS 0.93 (z=1.59, acc +0.93), BBB 1.16 (z=1.68, acc +0.86), both 95th-96th percentile; CCC 13.17, +432bp YTD.
NVDA fell 4.3% into a +7.5% SOXX session — -22.1% on the month, 19th percentile of its range, 12.6% below its 200-day. The AI complex is rallying without its leader.
The cycle keeps marking down: Brent -2.6% to 90.12 (-13.9% on the month), copper -0.8% and -5.5%, gold/silver z=1.82, DBC -6.0% — demand-side weakness, not supply.
Crypto refused the squeeze for a second day and accelerated lower: ETH -3.5% (-18.8% on the month), SOL -3.4% (-24.8%), BTC 73,798, COIN at the 0.7th percentile, MSTR -18.6%.
Volatility rose while equities rose: VIX +1.8% to 20.28 at z=1.41 and turning up, VIX/VIX3M z=1.61 out of inversion, SKEW 150 — the tape is paying up for a hedge it hasn't bought.
Brazil is the clearest stress point on a flat-dollar day: USD/BRL +1.1% to 5.5653 (z=3.14, acc +2.38), EWZ -25.1% on the month, Bovespa acceleration -3.84.

trades.name: Own the rotation, rent nothing in the index
trades.line: Long equal-weight S&P vs short QQQ into the beta squeeze
trades.expr: Long RSP (SPW) vs short QQQ, dollar-neutral, sized 1:1. Use the 11/9 pop in QQQ (+3.5%) as the entry level rather than averaging in.
trades.thesis: The regime shift under the index is intact and extreme: equal-weight/cap-weight z=3.59 with acceleration 3.28, Nasdaq/S&P z=-2.57 at the 18th percentile, growth/value at the 7th percentile, MTUM z=-3.01. Mega-cap tech is being distributed into strength while the median stock makes highs.
trades.trigger: QQQ +3.5% and SOXX +7.5% on 11/9 with NVDA -4.3% and GOOGL -18.1% on the month — the bounce is short covering without leadership, while SPW is +3.7% on the month versus SPX -3.3%.
trades.stop: QQQ/SPY reclaims its 200-day (above 0.933) and RSP/SPY z falls under 1.0, or SMH/SPY turns back up with NVDA reclaiming its 200-day.
trades.target: Another 6-8% of relative outperformance; QQQ/SPY toward 0.86.

trades.name: Make HY mark the credit tape
trades.line: Short HYG vs long IEF — spreads widening, HYG hasn't marked it
trades.expr: Short HYG against long IEF, equal dollars. Alternative expression: buy 3-month HYG puts ~5% OTM funded by selling upside calls.
trades.thesis: Credit is the one market telling the truth. IG OAS 0.93 at z=1.59 with acceleration +0.93 and BBB 1.16 at z=1.68 are both at the 95th-96th percentile of the year and widened through a +2.3% S&P day; CCC is +88bp on the month. HYG is +0.4% on the month and is pricing none of it, with HYG/IEF at z=-1.66.
trades.trigger: Today's spread set widened again while equities squeezed a fourth day, and the credit & vol composite is -48, the worst reading on the board.
trades.stop: HY OAS tightens back through 3.10 and IG back under 0.85 with BBB acceleration going negative.
trades.target: HY OAS toward 4.00; roughly 5% on the pair.

trades.name: Energy equity catch-down
trades.line: Short XOP/OIH against a 90-handle Brent that keeps falling
trades.expr: Short XOP (2/3) and OIH (1/3). Express tail risk with Feb XOP puts if you want convexity around OPEC headlines.
trades.thesis: Crude has broken and the equities haven't. Brent -13.9% and WTI -7.5% on the month with RBOB -21.0% at z=-1.94, yet XOP is only -9.1% on the month and still 1.8% above its 200-day, and XLE is +41.3% YTD at 5.6% above its 200-day. Either crude rebases higher or energy earnings estimates come down.
trades.trigger: Brent -2.6% today to 90.12 and -13.0% on the week, DBC -6.0% on the month at z=-1.44, while XOP was up on the squeeze day (+0.2%) and OIH +1.2%.
trades.stop: Brent closes back above 95 or RBOB z recovers above -0.5; cut on an 8% adverse move.
trades.target: 12% on the short basket; XOP toward its 3-month lows as it converges to crude.

trades.name: LatAm divergence: Mexico over Brazil
trades.line: Long EWW vs short EWZ as USD/BRL goes vertical
trades.expr: Long EWW vs short EWZ, equal dollars. If you can only do one leg, short EWZ and hedge with long USD/BRL forwards.
trades.thesis: Brazil is the one genuine stress point in EM and it is accelerating on a day the dollar isn't even strong: USD/BRL 5.5653, +10.9% on the month at z=3.14 with acceleration +2.38, EWZ -25.1% on the month, Bovespa acceleration -3.84. Mexico is the mirror image — IPC at the 100th percentile of its year, EWW +7.8% on the month with acceleration +1.53 and USD/MXN up only 2.2%.
trades.trigger: USD/BRL +1.1% today with DXY +0.1%; EWZ relative strength -22.5% over a month versus EWW +11.5%.
trades.stop: USD/BRL back below 5.30 with EWZ reclaiming its 200-day, or USD/MXN above 19.50 signalling broad LatAm contagion.

trades.name: India over the EM index
trades.line: Long INDA vs short EEM — the only EM compounding with its FX
trades.expr: Long INDA vs short EEM, equal dollars. Avoid adding Korea/Taiwan exposure elsewhere in the book while this is on.
trades.thesis: India is the single EM where equities and currency are improving together: INDA +11.7% on the month at z=2.66 with acceleration +2.76, Sensex +11.9%, USD/INR -3.0% at z=-2.91. EEM is -8.6% on the month and structurally long the semiconductor complex that just broke — EWY -19.8%, EWT -16.3%, KOSPI -20.9% on the month.
trades.trigger: EEM/SPY z=-1.28 at the 15th percentile while INDA's acceleration prints +2.76; the 11/9 Asia squeeze lifted Korea 3.7% and Taiwan 7.2%, giving a better short entry in EEM.
trades.stop: USD/INR back above 95.5 or EWY/EWT relative strength turning positive on a one-month basis.

trades.name: Crypto won't join the party
trades.line: Short ETH and COIN into a fourth day of equity squeeze
trades.expr: Short ETH spot/perp (70%) and short COIN equity (30%). Keep it small and dated — this is the liquidity tell, not a structural view.
trades.thesis: Crypto is the cleanest read on marginal risk appetite and it has now declined for two sessions through the strongest equity squeeze in months. ETH -3.5% today and -18.8% on the month, SOL -24.8%, ETH/BTC at the 20th percentile, COIN at the 0.7th percentile of its 52-week range, MSTR -18.6% on the month. With RRP at $0.25bn and bank reserves -2.1% over three months, there is no incremental dollar to bid it.
trades.trigger: BTC -1.9% to 73,798 and ETH -3.5% on a day Asia and Europe rallied 1-4%; crypto's relative strength versus the S&P is -8.8% (BTC) and -16.0% (ETH) over a month.
trades.stop: BTC closes above 80,000 with ETH/BTC turning up; cut on a 12% adverse move on the basket.
